newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends lower.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate finished lower on Monday on maturation of T$10 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit as dealers said short-term rates would be determined by the central bank's attitude.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 6.081 percent against Saturday's 6.182 close, still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with 30-day commercial paper stable at 6.00 percent.
In an apparent strategy to cool the red-hot stock market, central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said the bank would continue to issue NCDs to mop up banking system liquidity.
On Monday, the central bank issued T$5 billion in three-month NCDs at an average yield of 6.069 percent.
The bond market reported no trade in afternoon session as investors adopted a wait-and-see attitude amid stock market's bull run.
